references.text: The crowd meets Jesus again in Jerusalem after he has performed a sign (the raising of Lazarus), just as in 12:18. In both cases, it is the large crowd's reaction to a miracle that drives the action.

Here it is described that many of the Jews who had come to Mary saw what Jesus had done (the raising of Lazarus) and believed in him. This is the direct reason why the crowd meets Jesus in 12:18, since they have heard about this sign.

A similar situation where a large crowd follows Jesus because they have seen the signs he performed on the sick. This shows a recurring motif in the Gospel of John that crowds meet Jesus on the basis of his signs.
